title: Hybrid artifact cache + delta Dockerfile fast-path to cut CI latency
creator: Anya Patel
description: Problem: Pipelines frequently rebuild large service images and re-run identical dependency installs, causing long CI runtimes and noisy cache misses. Goal: Implement a hybrid artifact cache (local priming + S3-backed remote cache) paired with a delta-Dockerfile fast-path that only rebuilds changed layers and leverages dependency fingerprinting. Deliverables: (1) s3-cache adapter and cache key spec, (2) local priming job for most-used artifacts, (3) delta-Dockerfile generator that computes changed file fingerprints and emits minimal Dockerfile changes, (4) CI pipeline integration and opt-in flag for teams. Success metrics: median pipeline runtime for small changes < 6m (current ~14m), cache hit-rate >= 85% for PRs touching single package, reduced egress to container registry by 40% on nightly CI. Backwards compatibility: existing pipelines continue to run; opt-in gated by repository config file.
acceptance_criteria: S3-backed cache implemented and reachable from CI runners
Local cache priming job reduces cold-start misses for top 50 artifacts
Delta-Dockerfile fast-path used when file fingerprint set is unchanged for unrelated layers
Documented cache-key scheme and failure fallback to existing build path
Observed median PR pipeline runtime improvement in canary repos
comments: 2025-02-10 - Anya Patel: Created ticket after spike showed repeated NPM/Yarn installs cause most CI time. Proposal: hybrid cache + delta Dockerfiles to avoid full image rebuilds.

2025-02-14 - Diego Ramos: Implemented prototype s3 adapter using signed URLs; initial upload/download mechanics validated on staging runners. Link to draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4567
2025-02-18 - QA: Early benchmark on 'auth-service' shows full pipeline time 14m -> 9.5m with only s3 cache; misses still common for node_modules due to lockfile churn.

2025-02-21 - Diego Ramos: Introduced dependency fingerprinting that combines checksum of package-lock + relevant src paths. Local priming job scheduled as cron on CI fleet to populate hot artifacts each night. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ci-tools/pull/78

2025-02-25 - Design review (PM & Eng): Agreed to make delta-Dockerfile generator opt-in per-repo by adding .ci/delta-config.yml. Risk: incorrect fingerprinting could skip needed rebuilds — fallback must be robust.

2025-02-28 - Perf: Canary run on three repos (auth-service, console, runtime-agent) using hybrid cache + delta fast-path. Median PR time: auth-service 5:40, console 6:05, runtime-agent 7:10. Hit-rate measured 82% averaged. Need more runs to stabilize numbers.
2025-03-01 - Security: KMS key rotation considered for S3 uploads; scoped IAM roles created for CI runners with least privilege. Security review ticket created: PM-4183

2025-03-03 - Infra note: Observed transient 403s from S3 signed URLs under high concurrency; mitigation implemented by retry/backoff and batching small uploads into tarballs. Monitoring alert added: ci.s3cache.errors > 0.5%

2025-03-04 - Diego Ramos: Opened final PR to wire delta fast-path into pipeline with feature flag 'CI_DELTA_FASTPATH=true'. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ci-templates/pull/112. Requesting review from @maria-cho and @kevin-zhou.

2025-03-04 - Anya Patel: Next steps: broaden canary to 10 repos, add e2e test covering cache corruption and fallback, add docs and on-call runbook for cache incidents. Target full rollout in release ci-2025.03.
implementation_notes: Delta generator computes checksums for COPY/ADD sources and maps them to Dockerfile layers. When only non-layer files change, generate a no-op layer patch to avoid rebuilds.
Fallback path: any cache miss or verification failure falls back to canonical build and logs an annotated telemetry event.
Priming job will use most-frequent artifact list from Grafana query ci.artifact.popularity to avoid priming low-value items.
